story:
If you've ever been in my mom's kitchen, you already know this one. With a whiff of bliss, you are thrown into a row of jars cooling on the windowsill, and flour and baking powder on the walls. Every few minutes, one of the lids goes *ping*. The whole house smells like whatever's on the stove, plus a little of whatever was on it yesterday. She'll wave you in, hand you something warm, and keep working while you munch!

People ask where the recipes come from. Honestly, the recipes are newer; what Mom actually inherited was the shelf. Her mother never trusted an empty pantry: stocked deep, from canned collard greens to the sweetest of treats, both lay in like winter's always coming, because to her, a full shelf is how you tell the family it's safe. Mom has never let hers run thin either. Turns out that's hereditary. Holly's Pantry is the third generation of the same habit... We just started putting labels on the jars.

The business part is newer still, and honestly, it wasn't her idea. Left alone, she'd have kept feeding everyone for free forever. It took my dad, me, and pretty much everyone who ever went home with a jar of her pickles or dilly beans. That's where it really started. She gave those away for years, and every empty jar came back with the same request: more, and this time let us pay you. We've pulled her arm all the way to this point.

So here it is, just getting started. It runs the way a kitchen always has: come by, say hi, tell her what you're hungry for. She'd rather know what you need than guess at it. Call her at (406) 261-2772, she'll probably pick up :)
